name: Cyprus

facts.religion: Greek Orthodox about 75% in the south, Sunni Muslim in the north

snapshot: The far-right ELAM doubled its seats in May 2026's parliamentary election, and a YouTuber's new party got in too, as Cyprus held the EU presidency.
culture: Cyprus is said to be Aphrodite's birthplace, and its culture blends Greek, Turkish, Venetian and British influences. Halloumi cheese, meze and village festivals are central. The island has been divided since 1974, when Turkey invaded after a Greek-backed coup, and the Green Line runs through Nicosia, the last divided capital in Europe.
society: The Republic of Cyprus, in the south, is an EU member with an economy built on tourism, shipping and finance, including a history of hosting Russian money. The north, recognised only by Turkey, depends on Ankara. Reunification talks have been stalled since 2017. Migration across the Green Line has become a political issue.
situation: Cyprus has been divided since 1974, when Turkey invaded after a Greek-backed coup, and Turkish troops still hold the north. That wound shapes everything. In 2026 the island's parliamentary election showed it being reopened by a party that wants no compromise.

On 24 May, the conservative Democratic Rally came first with 17 seats and the communist AKEL second, each keeping exactly what they won in 2021. The story was underneath. ELAM, a far-right party founded as an offshoot of Greece's neo-Nazi Golden Dawn, doubled its seats to eight with nearly 11 percent, campaigning on migration, national identity and a harder line toward Turkey (National Herald). Two newcomers also entered: the anti-corruption ALMA, and Direct Democracy, founded months earlier by Fidias Panayiotou, a YouTuber who was elected to the European Parliament in 2024 and promises to let citizens direct their MPs through an app. The two old parties took 51 percent between them, down from nearly 69 percent in 2001, and the centrist parties backing President Nikos Christodoulides lost most of their seats (Who Governs). Because Cyprus is presidential, the vote did not change the government, but it is a clear warning before the 2028 presidential race. The 24 seats reserved for Turkish Cypriots have stood empty since the 1960s breakdown, a reminder of the island's other half.
power: A presidential republic. The president, directly elected for five years, is head of state and government and appoints ministers; the House of Representatives legislates but cannot bring down the government. The Republic's authority does not extend to the Turkish-controlled north.
holders: President Nikos Christodoulides, in office since 2023.
